newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Prospect sale contingent on divestments - NZCC.
newsitem.headline: Prospect sale contingent on divestments - NZCC.

text.p: Wilson and Horton-linked consortium Radio Network will have to divest a "significant number" of stations as part of its purchase of the prospect group of stations, the Commerce Commission said on Monday.

Radio Network earlier this year secured Radio New Zealand's commercial network. It has now acquired from Britain's GWR Group Plc the Prospect group, which has 12 radio stations and the Independent Radio News network, for NZ$40 million.
Commerce Commission chairman Alan Bollard told National Radio the commission had cleared the acquisition subject to Radio Network selling a significant number of stations in Auckland and Hamilton.
He said he was satisfied the acquisition would not lead to any dominance in the local markets the businesses operated in.
The Radio Network -- formerly the government-owned Radio NZ Commercial -- is owned by a consortium of domestic and international media and communications operations.
With Wilson and Horton are radio, newspaper and outdoor advertising group Australian Provincial Newspapers, and US radio and television operator Clear Channel Communications.
It has 44 stations throughout New Zealand and its brands include Newstalk ZB, Classic Hits, ZM and community stations.
Radio Network chief executive Joan Withers declined comment on Monday on which stations would be sold, but said she was sure all stations sold would continue to operate.
Withers said although there would be synergies between the two businesses, no decisions would be made about their possible integration until after a further evaluation of the operations.
Responding to criticism of the deal by Alliance and Labour spokespeople Pam Corkery and Graham Kelly, she said there were no plans to extend the IRN service to Radio Network stations.
She also discounted the closure of the IRN service, which she said was a "significant earner".
"It is not something that we will be curtailing or cutting off," Withers told National Radio.
The GWR radio group bought Prospect from Brierley Investments in March for NZ$29.8 million. It also bid unsuccessfully for Radio NZ's commercial stations.
Radio Network chairman John Maasland said the move would raise and strengthen the profile of radio in New Zealand, and he anticipated other private radio stations would benefit.
Maasland said that Radio Network had made a very successful and positive transition from public to private ownership.
"The shareholders recognise the strength and enthusiasm of the Radio Network team, and are confident of their ability to develop a larger radio market in New Zealand."
